headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Haystack can use MCP/REST with broad egress while MinerU processes rich documents via MCP and APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, and MinerU also exposes an MCP server plus document inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if MinerU content is routed into Haystack prompts or tools. The profiles do not prove a default shared channel, so I avoid high, but the interaction is credible.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are forwarded into Haystack prompts or tool inputs without sanitization
IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or message bus
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints for the pair
Insert a content-sanitization step before Haystack consumes MinerU output
Use separate service accounts for each agent
Log and review any tool-call arguments crossing the boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text, while Haystack has broad network egress and can use MCP/REST. If sensitive documents processed by MinerU are passed to Haystack, Haystack may transmit them outward. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or direct file sharing, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF MinerU processes sensitive documents that are then sent to Haystack
IF Haystack is configured to forward retrieved content to external APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of the shared pipeline
Route only redacted excerpts from MinerU to Haystack
Restrict Haystack egress to approved destinations
Separate storage locations for raw documents and downstream prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents expose MCP, and Haystack can use REST APIs while MinerU supports concurrent multi-threaded inference and multiple instances. That overlap can create contention on shared mutable resources if they are pointed at the same backend or workspace. No locking or shared-resource isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream service or shared MCP resource
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or per-agent isolation
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces or tenants
Add external locking around shared resources
Run each agent against distinct MCP servers
Avoid concurrent writes to the same document store

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system and MinerU is a document-processing extractor, so MinerU output can plausibly become Haystack input for retrieval or synthesis. If Haystack treats extracted text as authoritative, errors in OCR or parsing can cascade into downstream answers. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction results are used by Haystack without verification
IF Haystack-generated answers are acted on downstream as factual
mitigations: Add a verification step before Haystack consumes extracted text
Require source-document citations in downstream outputs
Sample-check OCR and table extraction quality
Flag low-confidence MinerU outputs for manual review

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch anonymous usage statistics on Haystack and document content on MinerU. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so a compliance issue is not established. I cite both profiles because the pairwise assessment depends on their combined data handling, but the evidence is thin.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into MinerU and then forwarded through Haystack
IF the deployment imposes retention or residency rules not reflected in either profile
mitigations: Confirm the data-class policy before deployment
Block regulated data from the pair until reviewed
Document retention settings for both agents
Review vendor terms for residency and logging
